author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page
summary: A read-only page at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it named in full. All specialties render on one page with no pagination.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html renders every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name on a single page with no pagination
Each specialty is shown with every veterinarian holding it, each named by first name followed by last name (for example "Helen Leary")
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians beneath it
A veterinarian holding no specialty is absent from the page, because the page lists specialties rather than the veterinarian roster
The veterinarians under each specialty are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
notes: Inverse view of the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001). Listing every specialty the clinic knows -- including one held by no veterinarian -- requires reading the specialties store directly, not inverting the vet->specialty map (which only surfaces held specialties). No SpecialtyRepository exists yet; design to decide whether to add a specialty query or a repository. Read-only; no new domain terms.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Every element maps to an in-force pattern with direct precedent in the codebase, so this is a small addition rather than new ground. (1) 'Every specialty the clinic knows' is read from the specialties store via a new SpecialtyRepository that mirrors owner/PetTypeRepository exactly -- a Repository over a lookup-value aggregate root with a name-ordered @Query. This is the correct fix for the inversion problem: inverting the vet->specialty map only surfaces held specialties, so an unheld specialty (none in the current seed, but the schema and requirement allow it) would be dropped; reading the store directly lists all of them. (2) The page reuses VetController (a third @GetMapping for /specialties.html), the vet feature's public directory surface, per the PRD file_targets -- no separate controller. (3) Grouping each specialty with its veterinarians is response assembly (the Web-controller 'select the response' remit, same category as the existing addPaginationModel), NOT a business rule, so it does not breach the no-rule-in-controller bar. Full names render in Thymeleaf as ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}, matching vetList.html -- no Java name helper. Verified against source via native Read (PetTypeRepository, VetController, Vet, vetList.html); IDE oracle not consulted. Small system-design.md Contracts update applied (SpecialtyRepository row, VetController + Specialty rows gain REQ-VET-003). No ADR: adding a lookup repository mirroring an existing one is a straightforward implementation choice with no trade-off.
integration_points: VetController gains a SpecialtyRepository constructor dependency alongside the existing VetRepository; both are injected
GET /specialties.html adds a model attribute holding the ordered grouping of every specialty with its veterinarians; view name vets/specialtyList
Vets are read through the existing @Cacheable('vets') VetRepository.findAll() -- the specialty page reuses that cache rather than adding one
specialtyList.html follows the fragments/layout :: layout replace pattern from vetList.html and adds a 'specialties' navbar key

patterns.description: Repository over a lookup-value root with a name-ordered @Query -- the exact template for SpecialtyRepository (Pattern Catalog: Repository, in force; one per aggregate root)
addPaginationModel: existing inline view-assembly in this controller -- precedent that grouping-for-display is a controller responsibility, not a business rule
SSR template using fragments/layout and ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}; specialtyList.html mirrors it, iterating specialties then their vets with a #{none} branch for an empty specialty

risks.risk: A reviewer could read the specialty/vet grouping in VetController as a business rule and flag the no-rule-in-controller checklist item.
risks.mitigation: It is presentation assembly (selecting the response), structurally identical to the existing addPaginationModel; recommend a small immutable record (e.g. a specialty paired with its veterinarian list) to carry the grouping typed rather than a Map<String,Object>, keeping the unit understandable and the intent explicit. A typed Map<Specialty,List<Vet>> is an acceptable lighter alternative.

risks.risk: Vets under a specialty and specialties themselves must render in a stable, not arbitrary, order (acceptance criterion 5).
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository's @Query orders specialties by name; order the veterinarians under each specialty by a deterministic key (last name then first name). Do not rely on Set/HashSet iteration order.

risks.risk: Adding a second cache for specialties would extend the un-evicted 'vets' cache open question (system-design Open Questions #5) to a new region with no write path.
risks.mitigation: Do NOT annotate SpecialtyRepository @Cacheable -- mirror PetTypeRepository (uncached). Reuse the existing vets cache for the vet side only. This neither resolves nor worsens Open Question #5.

notes: No new domain terms (Specialty and Veterinarian already canonical in ubiquitous-language.md). No ModularityTest exists to satisfy; everything stays in the vet package. The i18n test walks templates against message bundles (REQ-LANG-002), so any new #{...} keys in specialtyList.html (e.g. a page heading, 'specialties' nav label) must be added to every messages bundle. No autofix records to audit.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test method names do not follow the `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` BDD naming school mandated by docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. Names like `showSpecialtyListHtml` and `showSpecialtyListGroupsVeterinariansBySpecialty` mirror the controller method name rather than stating what must be true. A future rename of the production method would break the test-as-specification link.
findings.fix: Rename the five methods: showSpecialtyListHtml -> theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldReturnHtml; showSpecialtyListGroupsVeterinariansBySpecialty -> theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansBySpecialty; showSpecialtyListNamesVeterinarianInFull -> theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldNameEachVeterinarianByFullName; showSpecialtyListIncludesSpecialtyWithNoVeterinarian -> theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldIncludeSpecialtiesHeldByNoVeterinarian; showSpecialtyListOmitsVeterinarianWithNoSpecialty -> theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty

findings.description: @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository is a new mock of an internal repository. docs/testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy states that new tests must reach for a real implementation or a hand-written double first; a framework stub is a conscious exception chosen only when neither fits. In @WebMvcTest context a @TestConfiguration providing a hand-written double (an anonymous implementation of SpecialtyRepository returning fixed data) is feasible and is the preferred approach for new code.
findings.fix: Replace @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository with a @TestConfiguration static inner class that provides a @Bean returning an anonymous SpecialtyRepository implementation whose findSpecialties() returns List.of(specialty("dentistry"), specialty("radiology"), specialty("surgery")). Remove the `given(this.specialties.findSpecialties())...` stub in @BeforeEach.

findings.description: The assertion `content().string(containsString("Linda Douglas"))` in showSpecialtyListGroupsVeterinariansBySpecialty verifies that Linda Douglas appears somewhere on the page but does not verify that she appears under the `surgery` heading. If the template emitted all vets in a flat header and then specialty sections, the assertion would pass incorrectly. Using stringContainsInOrder would anchor her name to its specialty context.

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: Three sentences in the REQ-VET-003 prose paragraph exceed the 30-word limit, violating the writing standard (sentences under 30 words; 70% under 20 words). Sentence 1 (~32 words): "The clinic also publishes its specialties the other way round, so staff can answer which veterinarians hold this specialty as readily as the veterinarian directory answers which specialties does this veterinarian hold.". Sentence 2 (~38 words): "Every specialty the clinic knows is listed by its stored name on a single page — no pagination — each shown with the veterinarians who hold it, and each such veterinarian named in full, first name then last name.". Sentence 3 (~38 words): "The page lists specialties, not the veterinarian roster: a veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty, and so is absent from the page; a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians beneath it.".
findings.fix: Replace the three sentences with: "The clinic also publishes its specialties the other way round. Staff can answer which veterinarians hold a given specialty as readily as the veterinarian directory answers the reverse. Every specialty the clinic knows is listed by name on a single page, with no pagination. Each specialty shows the veterinarians who hold it, named in full: first name then last name. The page lists specialties, not the veterinarian roster. A veterinarian holding no specialty is absent from the page. A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians beneath it."

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet package plus its templates and docs: a new SpecialtyRepository, one grouping method and a nested SpecialtyVets record in VetController, a new /specialties.html route, a menu item, and a template. No sensitive paths; the added constructor parameter is Spring-injected and existing wiring is unaffected.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the controller: specialties come name-ordered from the query, holders are matched by specialty name and sorted deterministically by last-then-first name, an empty specialty is still emitted and a vet with no specialty is never matched. Behavior matches the diff's description exactly; no inverted operator or hidden effect. Template reuses message keys (specialties, none, name, vets) that already exist in the bundle.

test_adequacy.note: Five new MockMvc tests drive the real /specialties.html render and assert on HTML output: stringContainsInOrder anchors the last-then-first grouping order, dentistry (held by nobody) is asserted present, and James Carter (no specialty) is asserted absent. They fail against a broken grouping or ordering, and the by-name matching is forced because test fixtures build fresh Specialty instances per vet.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved. The one declined tested-as-spec finding (keep @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository rather than a hand-written double) was accepted on the merits by the test-reviewer on re-review: the JpaRepository surface makes a double heavier not lighter, and it stays consistent with the sibling @MockitoBean VetRepository. Security's round-1 approval stands because round 2 touched only test and doc files.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, zero build retries. The change delivers exactly the REQ-VET-003 surface — a read-only specialty directory — and explicitly excludes managing vets or specialties per NG-2. No wandering past the triaged scope.

rationale: All five facets clear on a direct read of the hunks. A cohesive, read-only single-feature change whose controller logic and edge cases match the spec and whose tests exercise them. Confirm and merge; a quick read of VetController.groupVetsBySpecialty suffices.
